source.title: Discovering and Causally Validating Emotion-Sensitive Neurons in Large Audio-Language Models
source.authors: Xiu-Tian Zhao; Björn W. Schuller; Berrak Sisman

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own neuron-level emotion interventions, but does not test the listed claims about pole-level job counts, generalization across model scales, classic vision neurons, attribution graphs, or explanation scoring.
record.gate_note: The paper reports causal effects of emotion-selected neuron sets in speech emotion recognition. These findings concern neuron-level functional selectivity, but do not measure any listed version's specific claim. Table 1 results are retained as related findings; the agnostic-injection results and other analyses are not rows for the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study selects emotion-sensitive decoder MLP gate neurons in three audio-language models and measures the causal effect of zeroing or amplifying them on speech emotion recognition accuracy. It does not audit what share of neurons have one, two or unknown jobs (V1, V2). It does not examine vision neurons or superposition (V3, V4), build attribution graphs (V5), or write and score neuron explanations (V6, V7). Its finding, that small selected neuron sets have emotion-specific causal effects, relates to neuron-level selectivity but measures no version's construct. It fits better as T6 or a related finding than as a test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that compact emotion-sensitive neurons exist in Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, Kimi-Audio and Audio Flamingo 3, and that zeroing or amplifying them selectively impairs or steers emotion recognition. Mean-deviation and contrast selectors beat frequency, entropy and random selection. Label-free injection gives mixed results, and cross-dataset transfer is partial and uneven.
record.recipe_differences: The paper identifies decoder MLP gate neurons from emotion-conditioned activations and tests them through deactivation and gain-based steering in audio-language models; it does not use the original pole audit or explanation-testing procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Selector choice changes the results: the paper reports stronger self–cross patterns for MAD and ConAct than for LAP and LAPE. It also reports intervention-budget and steering-strength trade-offs, and uneven transfer across datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing MAD- or ConAct-selected neurons (0.5% of decoder MLP gates) cuts accuracy on the target emotion by 11–15 points, with near-zero cross-emotion change, in all three models. Amplifying them raises target-emotion accuracy by about 2–3 points. Random masks are near-neutral. LAP/LAPE selectors give weak or non-specific effects; LAP on Audio Flamingo 3 drops about 35 points on all emotions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In audio-language models, small selected sets of decoder MLP neurons have emotion-specific causal effects on speech emotion recognition, and this depends on the selector used.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The study evaluates a speech-emotion-recognition task and selected decoder SwiGLU MLP gate activations, not general-purpose neuron interpretability. Identification uses correctly answered items; the reported aggregate effects cover three datasets, and uncertainty estimates are not stated for Table 1. The authors also note that attention and audio–text fusion components and composition into higher-level circuits are outside the analysis.
record.rows_left_out: Agnostic injection results in Table 2 (dataset × model × strategy × gain), intervention-budget and identification-pool analyses in Figure 2, steering-strength results in Figure 3, layer distributions in Figure 4, and transfer plots in Figure 5 are not included. They are outside the listed claim versions; Table 2 additionally contains many separately reported conditions.

untested.parts: No pole-level audit of Qwen3-32B neurons.
No share of interpretable neurons in any model. The study only selects the top 0.5% of neurons per emotion in 7B-scale audio-language models.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
No comparison of architecture, regularization or tools against interpretable-neuron share.
No attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No explanations from activating examples tested on held-out firing.

record.verdict_notes: Row values match Table 1. States of cannot_determine with versions ['none'] are appropriate, since no version is measured. The RND rows are controls, not results. The Audio Flamingo 3 LAP rows show broad degradation, about −35 points on both self and cross. Kimi-Audio is listed as Kimi-Audio-7B-Instruct in Table 3, so the record's size for it could be set to 7B.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or estimates of the share with one job, two jobs, or unknown jobs.
No cross-model or scale estimates of interpretable-neuron shares; the tested models are audio-language models and the outcome is emotion recognition.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car analysis or test of pose, recursive generalization, or superposition.
No comparison of vision-model interpretability rates, tools, regularization, or architecture effects.
No attribution graphs or comparison with trained replacement models or reconstruction error.
No explanation written from activating examples and tested for predicting firing on separate examples.
No automated explanation scoring by simulating neuron activations on new text.
